references.text: The Letter to the Hebrews mentions the golden jar of manna that was kept in the ark of the covenant, a direct reference to what Moses commanded Aaron to do.
The testimony (the tablets of the law) were to be placed in the ark, just as the manna was to be preserved as a witness for future generations.
The description of the ark and the mercy seat where God would meet His people, the place 'before the Lord' where the manna was to be placed.
Explains the unit of measure omer as one-tenth of an ephah, the same amount of manna that was to be kept in the jar.
Aaron's staff was also to be placed before the testimony as a sign for future generations, parallel to the preservation of the manna.
Moses put the tablets of the law in the ark, the same place where the manna was to be preserved as a reminder for descendants.
Jesus promises to give the hidden manna to the one who overcomes, a spiritual parallel to the preserved manna from the wilderness journey.
